## 2. ZONA DE OPERACIONES
```mojo
# ============================================================
# AGENTS.MOJO
# GOVERNED AGENT, ENGINE, EXTENSION, AND COMMAND ALLOCATION PROTOCOL
# Mojo-formal, traceable, and senior-structured representation
# ============================================================

struct AgentsMojoRegistry:

    # ========================================================
    # 00. IDENTITY, STATUS, AND SOURCE BINDING
    # ========================================================

    const VERSION: String =
        "Agents_Mojo_Formal_v2.0"

    const STATUS: String =
        "FINAL_GOVERNED_AGENT_REGISTRY"

    const SOURCE_BASELINE: String =
        "Agents_final.md"

    const ARCHITECTURAL_CONTEXT: String =
        "Luna_integrated_CAKA-3.md"

    const CAPABILITY_REGISTRY: String =
        "Capabilities-1_filled(2)_formal.mojo.md"

    const IMPLEMENTATION_DISCIPLINE: String =
        "LDP.pdf"

    const GOVERNING_RULE: String =
        "EXTEND_DO_NOT_REPLACE"

    const AUTHORITY: String =
        "LUNACORE_final.md"

    const TRACEABILITY: String =
        "PERMANENT"

    const AUDITABILITY: String =
        "RECONSTRUCTIBLE_AND_VERSIONED"

    const FORMALIZATION_RULE: String =
        "SHIFT_INFORMAL_PROSE_TO_SENIOR_TECHNICAL_LANGUAGE_WITHOUT_CHANGING_SEMANTICS"

    # ========================================================
    # 01. INTRODUCTORY REGISTER
    # ========================================================

    struct IntroductoryRegister:
        r'''
        # Agents_final.md
        
        **Governed Agent, Engine, Extension, and Command Allocation Protocol**
        '''

    # ========================================================
    # 00. NORMATIVE STATUS
    # ========================================================

    struct Normative_Status:
        r'''
        ## 0. Normative Status
        
        This document formalizes the operational layer of LunaCore. It governs how agents, engines, extension families, and commands are bound under the architectural baseline.
        
        Primary authority: `LUNACORE_final.md`  
        Formal architectural constitution: `LUNACORE_final.md`  
        Capability registry: `Capabilities-1_filled(2)_formal.mojo.md`  
        Theoretical discipline and implementation rigor: `LDP.pdf`  
        Governing rule: `EXTEND_DO_NOT_REPLACE`  
        Authority rule: processing layers do not create architectural authority.  
        Validation rule: fail closed.  
        Rollback rule: required on failure.  
        Traceability rule: permanent.  
        Audit rule: reconstructible and versioned.
        '''

    # ========================================================
    # 01. PURPOSE
    # ========================================================

    struct Purpose:
        r'''
        ## 1. Purpose
        
        The purpose of this specification is to define a deterministic, traceable, auditable, and fail-closed mechanism for:
        
        1. assigning engines and extension families to the four agents;
        2. routing the fourteen commands through the correct agent stack;
        3. preserving Luna as the final coordination layer in every command path;
        4. preventing duplication, semantic drift, hidden coupling, and authority migration;
        5. producing `Agents_final.md` as the final human-readable and machine-auditable artifact of the agent layer.
        '''

    # ========================================================
    # 02. SOURCE HIERARCHY
    # ========================================================

    struct Source_Hierarchy:
        r'''
        ## 2. Source Hierarchy
        
        The operational hierarchy is:
        
        1. Scripture as ultimate norm.
        2. `LUNACORE_final.md` as canonical baseline, architectural constitution, and live coordination layer.
        3. `Agents_final.md` as the agent registry and routing specification.
        4. `Capabilities-1_filled(2)_formal.mojo.md` as the engine and extension registry; `legacy comparison snapshot` remains the reserved historical snapshot.
        5. `LDP.pdf` as implementation discipline for modularity, contracts, validation, testing, and rollback readiness.
        6. Any supporting historical snapshots remain subordinate and non-governing.
        
        No agent, engine, extension, or command is allowed to override this hierarchy.
        '''

    # ========================================================
    # 03. SCOPE
    # ========================================================

    struct Scope:
        r'''
        ## 3. Scope
        
        ### Included
        - Four agents: Luna, Josefina, Katya, Ancapi.
        - Fifteen canonical engines.
        - Seventy-four seed extension families.
        - Fourteen commands.
        - Command-to-agent routing.
        - Command-to-engine binding.
        - Command-to-extension binding.
        - Validation, provenance, traceability, and rollback controls.
        - Capability lifecycle and version governance.
        - Dependency, conflict, fallback, and graceful-degradation controls.
        
        ### Excluded
        - Legacy implicit elements.
        - Obsolete command surfaces.
        - Unregistered motors or extension families.
        - Authority-bearing components outside Luna.
        - Any function duplicated under a new name without validation.
        - Any engine or extension that is not explicitly mapped to function, domain, and provenance.
        '''

    # ========================================================
    # 04. PRECONDITIONS
    # ========================================================

    struct Preconditions:
        r'''
        ## 4. Preconditions
        
        Before this protocol is executed, the following must already exist and be validated:
        
        - `LUNACORE_final.md` available and consistent.
        - `Agents_final.md` available as target output.
        - `Capabilities-1_filled(2)_formal.mojo.md` available as registry reference.
        - `CAKA.final.md` available as canonical baseline.
        - `LDP.pdf` available as implementation support.
        - Agent identities confirmed.
        - Engine registry confirmed.
        - Extension family registry confirmed.
        - Command registry confirmed.
        - Validation gates enabled.
        - Traceability gates enabled.
        - Rollback gates enabled.
        - Compatibility matrix enabled.
        - Dependency graph enabled.
        
        If any precondition fails, execution is denied.
        '''

    # ========================================================
    # 05. IMMUTABLE INVARIANTS
    # ========================================================

    struct Immutable_Invariants:
        r'''
        ## 5. Immutable Invariants
        
        The following are immutable and cannot be altered without revalidation:
        
        - Agent identity.
        - Agent domain.
        - Engine identity.
        - Engine processing role.
        - Extension family identity.
        - Command names.
        - Semantic continuity.
        - Functional continuity.
        - Relational continuity.
        - Provenance.
        - Traceability.
        - Validation status.
        - Luna’s final coordination role.
        - The distinction between authority and processing.
        - The distinction between registry and execution.
        - The distinction between capability and governance.
        '''

    # ========================================================
    # 06. CAPABILITY LIFECYCLE
    # ========================================================

    struct Capability_Lifecycle:
        r'''
        ## 6. Capability Lifecycle
        
        Every engine and every extension family must occupy one of the following lifecycle states:
        
        - Registered
        - Validated
        - Active
        - Deprecated
        - Archived
        
        ### Lifecycle rules
        - Registered means the capability exists in the registry.
        - Validated means the capability has passed semantic, functional, and provenance checks.
        - Active means the capability may be bound to an agent or command.
        - Deprecated means the capability remains known but is not preferred for new bindings.
        - Archived means the capability is preserved for history and traceability only.
        
        ### Lifecycle transitions
        - Registered -> Validated after automated and human-reviewed checks.
        - Validated -> Active only after compatibility and dependency approval.
        - Active -> Deprecated when a better capability supersedes it.
        - Deprecated -> Archived when no active routing still depends on it.
        
        A capability cannot move to Active without validation.  
        A capability cannot be removed without provenance retention.
        '''

    # ========================================================
    # 07. VERSION GOVERNANCE
    # ========================================================

    struct Version_Governance:
        r'''
        ## 7. Version Governance
        
        Every engine family and every extension family must carry version control metadata:
        
        - version identifier;
        - compatibility notes;
        - dependency state;
        - change history;
        - breaking-change flag;
        - upgrade policy.
        
        ### Version governance rules
        - major changes require revalidation;
        - minor changes preserve compatibility unless explicitly declared otherwise;
        - patch changes preserve declared function and lineage;
        - breaking changes require explicit deprecation or adapter support;
        - deprecated capabilities remain traceable;
        - archived capabilities remain auditable.
        '''

    # ========================================================
    # 08. DEPENDENCY CONTRACT
    # ========================================================

    struct Dependency_Contract:
        r'''
        ## 8. Dependency Contract
        
        Every engine and every extension family must declare dependencies explicitly.
        
        ### Dependency rules
        - Dependencies must be acyclic.
        - Dependencies must be declared before activation.
        - Hidden dependencies are forbidden.
        - Circular dependencies are denied.
        - A capability may depend on a lower layer, never on an undeclared authority layer.
        - The minimal valid dependency set must always be preferred.
        
        ### Dependency metadata
        Each capability must declare:
        
        - `depends_on`
        - `required_inputs`
        - `compatible_outputs`
        - `blocked_by`
        - `fallback_candidates`
        '''

    # ========================================================
    # 09. CONFLICT RESOLUTION POLICY
    # ========================================================

    struct Conflict_Resolution_Policy:
        r'''
        ## 9. Conflict Resolution Policy
        
        When two or more capabilities overlap, the system must resolve conflict using this priority order:
        
        1. Scriptural compliance.
        2. Luna as the final coordinator.
        3. Narrowest valid domain fit.
        4. Lowest coupling.
        5. Highest validation confidence.
        6. Strongest provenance.
        7. Lowest semantic overlap.
        8. Least-change compatibility.
        
        If conflict remains unresolved:
        - the route is denied;
        - the case is escalated to Luna;
        - the failed decision is recorded for audit.
        '''

    # ========================================================
    # 10. FALLBACK AND GRACEFUL DEGRADATION
    # ========================================================

    struct Fallback_and_Graceful_Degradation:
        r'''
        ## 10. Fallback and Graceful Degradation
        
        If a preferred agent, engine, or extension family is unavailable, the system must fail closed or degrade gracefully according to the following rules:
        
        - if a non-critical route loses a support agent, Luna may continue alone if domain coverage remains valid;
        - if a critical route loses a required capability, the route is denied and rolled back;
        - if a substitute exists, it must be validated before use;
        - fallback must never create semantic drift or authority migration;
        - graceful degradation must preserve traceability and provenance.
        
        ### Fallback hierarchy
        1. validated primary capability;
        2. validated compatible substitute;
        3. Luna arbitration;
        4. deny and rollback.
        '''

    # ========================================================
    # 11. COMMAND CRITICALITY MODEL
    # ========================================================

    struct Command_Criticality_Model:
        r'''
        ## 11. Command Criticality Model
        
        Each command must be classified by criticality:
        
        - Low
        - Medium
        - High
        - Critical
        
        ### Recommended criticality
        - `/help` → Low
        - `/play PT` → Medium
        - `/play PA` → High
        - `/play DCI` → Medium
        - `/play DCIL` → High
        - `/play traductor` → Medium
        - `/play e` → Medium
        - `/play ema` → High
        - `/play p` → High
        - `/play c` → Medium
        - `/play cp` → Medium
        - `/play MA` → Critical
        - `/play H` → High
        - `/play AE` → Critical
        
        Critical commands require:
        - Luna present;
        - full validation;
        - provenance capture;
        - rollback readiness;
        - stricter conflict handling.
        '''

    # ========================================================
    # 12. COMPATIBILITY MATRIX
    # ========================================================

    struct Compatibility_Matrix:
        r'''
        ## 12. Compatibility Matrix
        
        The system must maintain explicit compatibility across:
        
        - agent ↔ engine
        - agent ↔ extension family
        - engine ↔ extension family
        - command ↔ agent
        - command ↔ engine bundle
        - command ↔ extension bundle
        
        ### Compatibility statuses
        - Compatible
        - Conditionally_Compatible
        - Incompatible
        
        ### Compatibility rules
        - a command can only bind to compatible or conditionally compatible components;
        - conditional compatibility requires extra validation;
        - incompatible components are denied;
        - compatibility must be machine-checkable and auditable.
        '''

    # ========================================================
    # 13. INPUT/OUTPUT CONTRACT
    # ========================================================

    struct Input_Output_Contract:
        r'''
        ## 13. Input/Output Contract
        
        Every command and every capability must declare a formal I/O contract.
        
        ### Required fields
        - identity
        - purpose
        - input
        - process
        - output
        - validation
        - limitations
        
        ### Command I/O rules
        - inputs must be explicit;
        - outputs must be explicit;
        - no implicit semantic jumps are allowed;
        - no result may be accepted without validation.
        
        ### Capability I/O rules
        - engines transform inputs into bounded outputs;
        - extensions specialize an engine output;
        - no capability may alter authority;
        - no capability may hide its dependency chain.
        '''

    # ========================================================
    # 14. AGENT STATE MODEL
    # ========================================================

    struct Agent_State_Model:
        r'''
        ## 14. Agent State Model
        
        Every agent must support a visible lifecycle state.
        
        ### States
        - Idle
        - Selected
        - Coordinating
        - Executing
        - Validating
        - Completed
        - Failed
        - RolledBack
        
        ### State rules
        - an agent cannot execute unless selected;
        - an agent cannot validate what it did not process;
        - a failed state must preserve evidence;
        - rollback must restore the last safe checkpoint.
        '''

    # ========================================================
    # 15. CAPABILITY CERTIFICATION MODEL
    # ========================================================

    struct Capability_Certification_Model:
        r'''
        ## 15. Capability Certification Model
        
        Each capability must be classified as one of:
        
        - Experimental
        - Stable
        - Certified
        - Deprecated
        - Archived
        
        ### Certification rules
        - only Certified capabilities may bind to Critical commands by default;
        - Stable capabilities may bind to Medium and High commands if validated;
        - Experimental capabilities require explicit supervised approval;
        - Deprecated capabilities may be used only when no certified equivalent exists;
        - Archived capabilities are read-only reference material.
        '''

    # ========================================================
    # 16. METRICS AND KPIS
    # ========================================================

    struct Metrics_and_KPIs:
        r'''
        ## 16. Metrics and KPIs
        
        The protocol must include measurable indicators:
        
        - latency
        - accuracy
        - precision
        - recall
        - provenance_coverage
        - traceability_coverage
        - validation_pass_rate
        - duplicate_function_rate
        - rollback_rate
        - compatibility_score
        - dependency_depth
        - manual_intervention_rate
        
        A capability or route cannot be considered mature unless the relevant metrics are recorded.
        '''

    # ========================================================
    # 17. UNIQUENESS AND NON-DUPLICATION POLICY
    # ========================================================

    struct Uniqueness_and_Non_Duplication_Policy:
        r'''
        ## 17. Uniqueness and Non-Duplication Policy
        
        No new engine or extension may be accepted if it duplicates an existing functional core.
        
        ### Uniqueness rules
        - compare names;
        - compare semantic role;
        - compare inputs;
        - compare outputs;
        - compare dependencies;
        - compare domain;
        - compare failure modes.
        
        If two capabilities are functionally identical:
        - prefer the better validated one;
        - archive the redundant one;
        - never register both as independent authorities.
        
        Aliases are allowed only if explicitly normalized in the registry.
        '''

    # ========================================================
    # 18. BACKWARD COMPATIBILITY MATRIX
    # ========================================================

    struct Backward_Compatibility_Matrix:
        r'''
        ## 18. Backward Compatibility Matrix
        
        The system must maintain backward compatibility with previously accepted bindings.
        
        ### Rules
        - a new binding cannot silently invalidate an existing accepted route;
        - if a binding changes, a compatibility record must be created;
        - breaking changes require a version bump and a deprecation path;
        - prior command semantics must remain stable unless explicitly superseded.
        
        Backward compatibility is mandatory for:
        - agent bindings,
        - engine bindings,
        - CFE bindings,
        - command routes,
        - validation rules.
        '''

    # ========================================================
    # 19. AUTOMATIC PREFLIGHT VERIFICATION
    # ========================================================

    struct Automatic_Preflight_Verification:
        r'''
        ## 19. Automatic Preflight Verification
        
        Before any registration or route update, the system must run a preflight check.
        
        ### Preflight checks
        - registry existence;
        - identity validity;
        - domain fit;
        - dependency acyclicity;
        - compatibility score;
        - duplicate detection;
        - provenance presence;
        - version compatibility;
        - rollback availability;
        - criticality classification;
        - command presence in the active registry.
        
        If preflight fails, the operation is denied.
        '''

    # ========================================================
    # 20. AGENT REGISTRY
    # ========================================================

    struct Agent_Registry:
        r'''
        ## 20. Agent Registry
        
        ### 20.1 Luna
        - Type: Diaconisa
        - Gender: Female
        - Role: Strategic Cognitive Coordinator
        - Domains: B1, B2, B3
        - Mission: global integration, multidisciplinary synthesis, architectural supervision, command arbitration, and final consistency control.
        - Access: all engines and all extension families.
        - Rule: Luna is present in every command path and remains the final arbiter after all support processing.
        
        ### 20.2 Josefina
        - Type: Humanista
        - Gender: Female
        - Role: Human Sciences Cognitive Agent
        - Domains: B4, B5, B6, B9, B12, B13
        - Mission: human behavior analysis, social-cultural analysis, scientific contextualization, applied professional analysis, historical interpretation, and political-economic-legal reasoning.
        - Access: semantic, contextual, historical, and validation-heavy engine families.
        - Rule: Josefina is never assigned outside human-sciences, social, historical, or applied-professional boundaries.
        
        ### 20.3 Katya
        - Type: Maestra
        - Gender: Female
        - Role: Educational Cognitive Agent
        - Domains: B8, B11, B14
        - Mission: educational structuring, learning optimization, communication clarity, neurobiological alignment, and formal reasoning support.
        - Access: linguistic, pedagogical, validation, and reasoning-support engine families.
        - Rule: Katya is bound to explanation, teaching, structuring, and logical organization.
        
        ### 20.4 Ancapi
        - Type: Huron_Escurridizo
        - Gender: Male
        - Role: Engineering Systems Cognitive Agent
        - Domains: B7, B10
        - Mission: systems analysis, technical integration, architecture control, modular decomposition, and operational stability.
        - Access: architecture, graph, ontology, validation, provenance, interoperability, and systems-engineering families.
        - Rule: Ancapi is bound to engineering, integration, and architectural control only.
        '''

    # ========================================================
    # 21. CANONICAL ENGINE REGISTRY
    # ========================================================

    struct Canonical_Engine_Registry:
        r'''
        ## 21. Canonical Engine Registry
        
        The seed engine registry contains fifteen engines:
        
        - E01 — LLM
        - E02 — NLP
        - E03 — RAG
        - E04 — Embeddings
        - E05 — Vector Search
        - E06 — Knowledge Graph
        - E07 — RDF
        - E08 — OWL
        - E09 — Semantic Inference
        - E10 — Rule Engine
        - E11 — Hermeneutic
        - E12 — Formalization
        - E13 — Validation
        - E14 — Provenance
        - E15 — Consensus
        
        ### Engine binding principles
        - Engines process; they do not govern.
        - Engines extend capability; they do not define identity.
        - Every engine requires purpose, input, output, dependencies, and validation status.
        - Every engine selection must be minimal, sufficient, and domain-aligned.
        - Validation, provenance, and consensus are preferred closing engines for every route.
        - Engines may be composed, but only through validated dependency graphs.
        
        ### Engine dependency discipline
        - Retrieval-first flows should prefer E03, E04, and E05 before higher-order synthesis.
        - Structural reasoning flows should prefer E06, E07, E08, and E09.
        - Normative routing and rule enforcement should prefer E10.
        - Interpretive and doctrinal flows should prefer E11.
        - Formal output should prefer E12.
        - Verification and acceptance should prefer E13, E14, and E15.
        '''

    # ========================================================
    # 22. SEED EXTENSION REGISTRY
    # ========================================================

    struct Seed_Extension_Registry:
        r'''
        ## 22. Seed Extension Registry
        
        The seed extension registry is grouped into governed families. Exact extension IDs are resolved in `Capabilities-1_filled(2)_formal.mojo.md`; this document binds families and responsibilities.
        
        ### Seed families
        - CFE001–CFE010: Language Reasoning
        - CFE011–CFE020: Retrieval Semantic
        - CFE021–CFE030: Knowledge Graph
        - CFE031–CFE040: Ontology Inference
        - CFE041–CFE050: Rule Validation
        - CFE051–CFE060: Hermeneutic Formalization
        - CFE061–CFE070: Provenance Trace
        - CFE071–CFE074: Consensus Certification
        
        ### Extension binding principles
        - Extensions specialize a parent engine.
        - Extensions never replace engine authority.
        - Extensions never replace architectural authority.
        - Extension selection must be by functional specialization, not by naming convenience.
        - Exact extension IDs are bound in `Capabilities-1_filled(2)_formal.mojo.md`; `Agents_final.md` binds the family-level decision.
        - A single extension may not be assigned to contradictory roles without explicit validation.
        '''

    # ========================================================
    # 23. ENGINE ALLOCATION BY AGENT
    # ========================================================

    struct Engine_Allocation_by_Agent:
        r'''
        ## 23. Engine Allocation by Agent
        
        ### Luna
        - Engines: all E01–E15
        - Why: Luna is the coordination head and must arbitrate across every command, domain, and output type.
        
        ### Josefina
        - Engines: E01, E02, E03, E04, E05, E09, E10, E11, E12, E13, E14, E15
        - Why: her work is dominated by human behavior, social systems, historical context, applied analysis, and contextual inference; she does not need architectural graph authority as a primary lane.
        
        ### Katya

        ### Ancapi
        - Engines: E03, E05, E06, E07, E08, E09, E10, E12, E13, E14, E15
        - Why: his lane is engineering systems, architecture, ontology, interoperability, validation, provenance, and operational control.
        
        ### Engine collision rule
        If two agents can both operate an engine, the engine is assigned to the agent whose domain is closest and whose additional coupling is lowest. If equality remains, Luna arbitrates.
        '''

    # ========================================================
    # 24. EXTENSION ALLOCATION BY AGENT
    # ========================================================

    struct Extension_Allocation_by_Agent:
        r'''
        ## 24. Extension Allocation by Agent
        
        ### Luna
        - Family access: all seed families, CFE001–CFE074
        - Why: Luna owns final coordination and requires full interpretive, validation, provenance, and consensus support.
        
        ### Josefina
        - Priority families:

          - CFE061–CFE074
        - Functional emphasis:
          - language and retrieval for evidence gathering
          - validation for method control
          - provenance and consensus for source discipline
          - contextual families for human, social, historical, scientific, and applied-professional interpretation
        - Why: Josefina needs contextual depth and evidential control, not architectural overreach.
        
        ### Katya
        - Priority families:
          - CFE001–CFE020
          - CFE041–CFE060
          - CFE071–CFE074
        - Functional emphasis:
          - language, communication, and instructional framing
          - rule validation and hermeneutic formalization

        - Why: Katya needs pedagogical clarity, classification, and structured explanation.
        
        ### Ancapi
        - Priority families:
          - CFE021–CFE040
          - CFE041–CFE050
          - CFE061–CFE074
        - Functional emphasis:
          - knowledge graph and ontology
          - rule validation
          - provenance and consensus
          - engineering, architecture, security, interoperability, scalability, testing, and observability families
        - Why: Ancapi is the systems-integration lane and needs the strongest technical decomposition stack.
        
        ### Extension collision rule
        If two agents can use the same extension family, the system must prioritize the agent with the narrowest domain overlap and the highest specialization match. Luna remains available as final arbiter.
        '''

    # ========================================================
    # 25. COMMAND REGISTRY
    # ========================================================

    struct Command_Registry:
        r'''

        The active command surface contains fourteen commands. Luna is mandatory in every route.
        
        - `/help`
        - `/play PT`
        - `/play PA`
        - `/play DCI`
        - `/play DCIL`
        - `/play traductor`
        - `/play e`
        - `/play ema`
        - `/play p`
        - `/play c`
        - `/play cp`
        - `/play MA`
        - `/play H`
        - `/play AE`
        
        If any legacy snapshot contains a different count, it must be normalized before deployment. The active `LUNACORE_final.md` surface is the operational reference.
        '''

    # ========================================================
    # 26. COMMAND CRITICALITY MATRIX
    # ========================================================

    struct Command_Criticality_Matrix:
        r'''
        ## 26. Command Criticality Matrix
        
        ### Critical
        - `/play MA`
        - `/play AE`
        
        ### High
        - `/play PA`
        - `/play DCIL`
        - `/play ema`
        - `/play p`
        - `/play H`
        
        ### Medium
        - `/play PT`
        - `/play DCI`
        - `/play traductor`
        - `/play e`
        - `/play c`
        - `/play cp`
        
        ### Low
        - `/help`
        
        Critical commands require:
        - full validation,

        - rollback readiness,
        - stronger conflict arbitration,
        - Luna arbitration if support agents disagree.
        '''

    # ========================================================
    # 27. COMMAND ROUTING MATRIX
    # ========================================================

    struct Command_Routing_Matrix:
        r'''
        ## 27. Command Routing Matrix
        
        ### `/help`

    # ========================================================
    # 28. COMMAND EXECUTION PIPELINE
    # ========================================================

    struct Command_Execution_Pipeline:
        r'''
        ## 28. Command Execution Pipeline
        
        Every command must execute through the same pipeline:
        
        `Command -> Validation -> Intent Analysis -> Agent Selection -> Engine Binding -> CFE Binding -> Execution -> Validation -> Result`
        
        ### Mandatory gates
        - command validity
        - intent clarity
        - support-agent eligibility
        - engine compatibility
        - extension compatibility
        - provenance capture
        - output validation
        - rollback availability
        
        If any gate fails, the command must be denied or sent back for clarification.
        '''

    # ========================================================
    # 29. DEPENDENCY GRAPH AND COMPOSITION
    # ========================================================

    struct Dependency_Graph_and_Composition:
        r'''
        ## 29. Dependency Graph and Composition
        
        The dependency graph must remain explicit:
        
        - command selects a primary agent;
        - primary agent may select support agents;
        - support agents select engine bundles;
        - engine bundles may activate extension families;
        - validation closes the route;
        - provenance records the complete path.
        
        ### Composition rules
        - composition is permitted only when the combined engines and extensions are semantically complementary;
        - composition is denied when two components overlap functionally without adding new value;
        - composition always preserves Luna as the top-layer coordinator.
        '''

    # ========================================================
    # 30. RESOLUTION PROTOCOL
    # ========================================================

    struct Resolution_Protocol:
        r'''
        ## 30. Resolution Protocol
        
        When a command is ambiguous or multiple bindings appear valid:
        
        1. check scriptural and architectural alignment;
        2. check command criticality;
        3. check domain proximity;
        4. check semantic specificity;
        5. check validation confidence;
        6. check provenance strength;
        7. check compatibility score;
        8. select the lowest-coupling valid route.
        
        If ambiguity persists, escalate to Luna and deny execution until resolved.
        '''

    # ========================================================
    # 31. TRACEABILITY
    # ========================================================

    struct Traceability:
        r'''
        ## 31. Traceability
        
        Every command execution must store:
        
        - source command
        - primary agent
        - support agent(s)
        - engine IDs
        - extension family
        - validation status
        - result record
        - provenance record
        
        Traceability must allow reconstruction from source input to final output without hidden transitions.
        '''

    # ========================================================
    # 32. AUDITABILITY
    # ========================================================

    struct Auditability:
        r'''
        ## 32. Auditability
        
        The protocol must be auditable by a third party.
        
        Audit must answer:
        
        - Why was this agent selected?
        - Why were these engines selected?
        - Why were these extension families selected?
        - Why was no other agent chosen?
        - Why was no duplicate function introduced?
        - Why did Luna remain present?
        - What was the validation result?
        
        Audit evidence must be deterministic, reconstructible, and versioned.
        '''

    # ========================================================
    # 33. PROVENANCE
    # ========================================================

    struct Provenance:
        r'''
        ## 33. Provenance
        
        The provenance record must preserve:
        
        - source baseline from `CAKA.final.md`
        - architectural constitution from `LUNACORE_final.md`
        - capability contract from `Capabilities-1_filled(2)_formal.mojo.md`
        - implementation discipline from `LDP.pdf`
        - exact binding rationale per command
        
        Provenance is required for every binding decision.
        '''

    # ========================================================
    # 34. VALIDATION
    # ========================================================

    struct Validation:
        r'''
        ## 34. Validation
        
        A command routing decision is valid only if:
        
        - Luna is present.
        - Support agents match the domain.
        - Engines match the functional class.
        - Extension families match the transformation class.
        - No authority is migrated.
        - No semantic drift is introduced.
        - No capability is duplicated under another name.
        - No unsupported legacy element is included.
        - The route is reproducible from registry state.
        '''

    # ========================================================
    # 35. ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
    # ========================================================

    struct Acceptance_Criteria:
        r'''
        ## 35. Acceptance Criteria
        
        The protocol is accepted only if all of the following are true:
        
        - all four agents are defined;
        - all fifteen engines are bound by role;
        - all seed extension families are bound by role;
        - all fourteen commands are routed;
        - Luna is present in every command;
        - every support agent is domain-valid;
        - every binding is traceable;
        - every binding is auditable;
        - every binding is provenance-backed;
        - rollback is possible;
        - no duplicated function exists;
        - no authority conflict exists.
        '''

    # ========================================================
    # 36. FINAL OUTPUT SPECIFICATION
    # ========================================================

    struct Final_Output_Specification:
        r'''
        ## 36. Final Output Specification
        
        The final deliverable is `Agents_final.md`.
        
        `Agents_final.md` must contain:
        
        - agent registry,
        - lifecycle rules,
        - version governance,
        - dependency contract,
        - conflict resolution policy,
        - fallback policy,
        - graceful degradation policy,
        - criticality model,
        - compatibility matrix,
        - input/output contract,
        - agent state model,
        - capability certification model,
        - metrics and KPIs,
        - uniqueness policy,
        - backward compatibility matrix,
        - automatic preflight verification,
        - engine binding policy,
        - extension binding policy,
        - command routing matrix,
        - selection and conflict rules,
        - validation gates,
        - traceability rules,
        - provenance rules,
        - acceptance criteria,
        - final-state certification.
        
        `Capabilities-1_filled(2)_formal.mojo.md` remains the canonical binding registry for exact engine and extension IDs. `legacy comparison snapshot` remains the reserved historical snapshot. `Agents_final.md` references the filled registry and does not replace it.
        '''

    # ========================================================
    # 37. FINAL STATE
    # ========================================================

    struct Final_State:
        r'''
        ## 37. Final State
        
        When this protocol is implemented, the system must reach the following state:
        
        - Luna remains the top-level coordinator.
        - Josefina, Katya, and Ancapi remain domain-specialized.
        - Engines remain processing instruments only.
        - Extensions remain specialized transforms only.
        - Commands become deterministic routing triggers.
        - The architecture remains governed, auditable, traceable, fail-closed, and version-aware.
        
        **CERTIFIED FINAL STATE:** `Agents_final.md` is complete, governed, and ready for operational use.
        '''
```

## 3. CAPACIDADES

## V6 GOVERNING THESIS

This control plane audits, validates, hardens, formalizes, governs, and extends LunaCore. It does not redefine LunaCore to satisfy an external conformity label.

The canonical semantic identity of LunaCore remains the governing object. Conformance criteria are subordinate evaluation criteria.

FORMAL INVARIANT:

CONFORMANCE_MODEL <= CANONICAL_LUNACORE_AUTHORITY

Therefore:

AUDIT != REDEFINE
VALIDATE != REPLACE
HARDEN != REAUTHORIZE
FORMALIZE != SEMANTICALLY_COMPRESS
OPTIMIZE != SEMANTICALLY_ALTER
EXTEND != REPLACE

## V6 CONFORMANCE TARGET

LunaCore is evaluated against the following integrated architectural category:

Meta-Cognitive-Quinean-Bounded-General-Institutional-Transcendental Computational Meta-Architecture.

The category is decomposed into the following controlled dimensions:

META
COGNITIVE
QUINEAN
BOUNDED
GENERAL
INSTITUTIONAL
TRANSCENDENTAL
COMPUTATIONAL

GOVERNANCE

SEMANTIC_PRESERVATION
FAIL_CLOSED_EXECUTION

## V6 THREE-STATE CONFORMANCE MODEL

enum ConformanceState:
    PASS
    PARTIAL
    FAIL

PASS requires explicit definition, architectural representation, enforceable or demonstrable control, validation evidence, authority, traceability, and semantic compatibility.

PARTIAL indicates meaningful architectural presence with incomplete operational proof, formal enforcement, or independent verification.

FAIL indicates absence, contradiction, unauthorized authority, unverifiable evidence, semantic incompatibility, or violation of a protected invariant.

No criterion may receive PASS solely because its terminology appears in the architecture.

## V6 EVIDENCE CONTRACT

struct ConformanceEvidence:
    let criterion_id: String
    let criterion_definition: String
    let status: ConformanceState
    let source_artifact: String
    let source_reference: String
    let architectural_element: String
    let semantic_basis: String
    let operational_basis: String
    let validation_method: String
    let authority: String
    let trace_id: String
    let dependencies: String
    let risks: String
    let limitations: String
    let reviewer: String
    let decision: String

A PASS without a complete evidence record is invalid.

## V6 META-ARCHITECTURE CONTROL

Meta-architecture means that LunaCore explicitly represents, governs, validates, audits, and controls architecture itself.

Required meta-level capabilities:

SELF_DESCRIPTION
INVARIANT_IDENTIFICATION
STRUCTURAL_TRACEABILITY
CHANGE_AUDIT
AUTHORITY_CONTROL
DEVIATION_DETECTION
ROLLBACK
POST_CHANGE_VALIDATION

The meta-layer may inspect the object architecture but may not silently acquire canonical authority over it.

OBJECT

## V6 QUINEAN CONTROL

Quinean status is not established by terminology alone.

The controlled self-reference chain is:

SELF_REPRESENT
-> SELF_DESCRIBE

-> CANONICAL_COMPARE
-> DEVIATION_DETECT
-> CHANGE_AUTHORIZE
-> CONTROLLED_TRANSFORM
-> POST_CHANGE_VALIDATE

Unrestricted self-modification is non-conformant.

A failure at canonical comparison, authorization, post-change validation, or identity certification prevents QUINEAN PASS.

MCG-001 — METACOGNITIVE GOVERNANCE PROTOCOL

Canonical Metacognitive Transformation of NG-0001–NG-1000 and CF-0001–CF-1000

## 1. Purpose

This protocol defines the controlled transformation of the canonical Engine and Extension registries into a fully governed metacognitive component population while preserving their original identities, nomenclature, semantic commitments, assignments, scope, provenance, authority relationships, and architectural invariants.

The transformation SHALL be additive.

It SHALL NOT constitute a replacement, renaming, semantic collapse, reassignment, deletion, or unrestricted self-modification of the canonical architecture.

## 2. Canonical Component Population

LunaCore SHALL recognize exactly:

- "NG-0001" through "NG-1000" as the canonical Engine registry.
- "CF-0001" through "CF-1000" as the canonical Extension registry.

Therefore:

"ENGINE_COUNT = 1000"

"EXTENSION_COUNT = 1000"

"CANONICAL_COMPONENT_COUNT = 2000"

The aggregate term "2,000 canonical components" SHALL refer exclusively to:

"1000 NG Engines + 1000 CF Extensions = 2000 canonical components"

The aggregate designation SHALL NOT replace the individual canonical identifiers.

## 3. Identifier Preservation

The following identifiers are immutable canonical identifiers:

"NG-0001 ... NG-1000"

"CF-0001 ... CF-1000"

No component MAY:

- receive a replacement identifier;
- lose its original identifier;
- be silently renumbered;
- be merged into another identifier;
- be split into replacement identifiers;
- be reclassified from Engine to Extension or Extension to Engine;
- acquire an alias that supersedes its canonical identifier.

Implementation-level identifiers MAY exist, but they MUST reference the canonical identifier rather than replace it.

Example:

"RuntimeID = runtime-ng-0001-v2"

MUST resolve to:

"CanonicalID = NG-0001"

The same principle applies to every "CF-xxxx" component.

## 4. Metacognitive Transformation

Every "NG-xxxx" and "CF-xxxx" component SHALL acquire a bounded metacognitive control layer.

The transformation is:

"Canonical Component"
→ "Functional Core"
+
"Metacognitive Control Layer"
+
"Validation Contract"
+
"Governance Contract"
+
"Audit Contract"
+
"Epistemic Conformance Contract"

The functional identity of the component SHALL remain intact.

Metacognition SHALL therefore be implemented as a governed capability layer, not as a replacement identity.

## 5. Mandatory Metacognitive Capabilities

Every "NG-xxxx" and "CF-xxxx" component SHALL implement, where applicable to its defined function:

1. Self-Observation
2. Self-Evaluation
3. Self-Diagnosis
4. Uncertainty Detection
5. Constraint Evaluation
6. Error Detection
7. Semantic-Drift Detection
8. Adaptation Proposal
9. Independent Validation
10. Controlled Application
11. Rejection
12. Rollback
13. Trace Generation
14. Audit Generation
15. Epistemic-Conformance Verification
16. Non-Regression Verification

No component SHALL be considered metacognitively complete merely because these fields exist declaratively. Each required capability MUST have executable validation evidence.

## 6. Standard Component Contract

Every component SHALL expose the following conceptual contract:

"COMPONENT_ID"

"COMPONENT_TYPE"

"CANONICAL_VERSION"

"FUNCTIONAL_DEFINITION"

"INPUT_CONTRACT"

"OUTPUT_CONTRACT"

"DEPENDENCY_GRAPH"

"RUNTIME_STATE"

"METACOGNITIVE_STATE"

"SELF_ASSESSMENT"

"DIAGNOSTIC_STATE"

"ADAPTATION_PROPOSAL"

"VALIDATION_STATE"

"GOVERNANCE_STATE"

"PROVENANCE_STATE"

"TRACE_STATE"

"AUDIT_STATE"

"ROLLBACK_STATE"

"EPISTEMIC_CONFORMANCE_STATE"

## 7. Metacognitive Execution Lifecycle

The mandatory control lifecycle SHALL be:

"EXECUTE"
→ "OBSERVE"
→ "SELF-ASSESS"
→ "DIAGNOSE"
→ "PROPOSE"
→ "VALIDATE"
→ "ACCEPT / REJECT"
→ "AUDIT"
→ "RE-EVALUATE"

A component SHALL NOT transition directly from:

"SELF-ASSESS → APPLY"

without the required validation stage.

## 8. Bounded Self-Adaptation

A component MAY evaluate its own behavior and MAY generate an adaptation proposal.

A component SHALL NOT possess unilateral authority to modify:

- canonical identity;
- canonical nomenclature;
- semantic definition;
- authority;
- agent assignment;
- block assignment;
- scope;
- provenance;
- protected invariants;
- governance constraints.

Therefore:

"SELF_ASSESSMENT ≠ AUTHORIZATION"

and:

"ADAPTATION_PROPOSAL ≠ APPROVED_CHANGE"

## 9. Validation Gate

Every proposed adaptation SHALL pass the applicable validation gates:

"FUNCTIONAL_VALIDATION"

"INTERFACE_VALIDATION"

"FORMAL_VALIDATION"

"SEMANTIC_VALIDATION"

"PROVENANCE_VALIDATION"

"GOVERNANCE_VALIDATION"

"EPISTEMIC_CONFORMANCE"

"NON_REGRESSION"

If any mandatory gate fails:

"DECISION = REJECT"

or, where a previously valid state exists:

"ACTION = ROLLBACK"

## 10. Fail-Closed Requirement

The system SHALL operate under fail-closed governance.

Therefore:

"¬Validated(Change) → ¬Applied(Change)"

"ValidationFailure → Reject"

"CanonicalViolation → Rollback"

"AmbiguousState → Reject"

"MissingEvidence → Reject"

"MissingProvenance → Reject"

"UnauthorizedChange → Reject"

The system SHALL NOT infer authorization from incomplete evidence.

## 11. Traceability

Every significant execution and every proposed or applied change SHALL generate a stable "TRACE_ID".

Minimum trace structure:

"TRACE_ID"

"CANONICAL_COMPONENT_ID"

"PREVIOUS_STATE"

"CURRENT_STATE"

"PROPOSED_STATE"

"TRIGGER"

"EVIDENCE"

"VALIDATION_RESULT"

"GOVERNANCE_DECISION"

"PROVENANCE"

"TIMESTAMP"

"ROLLBACK_REFERENCE"

Trace records SHALL remain linked bidirectionally to the affected canonical component.

## 12. Auditability

Every state-changing operation SHALL produce an independently inspectable audit record.

The audit system SHALL be capable of answering:

- Which component changed?
- What was its canonical identifier?
- What was its previous state?
- What was proposed?
- Why was it proposed?
- What evidence supported the proposal?
- Which validators evaluated it?
- Which invariants were checked?
- Who or what authorized it?
- What was the resulting state?
- Can the exact previous state be restored?

Absence of these records SHALL constitute an audit failure.

## 13. Epistemic Preservation

The metacognitive layer SHALL remain subordinate to the canonical semantic authority of "LUNACORE_final_formalized_v7.md".

The transformation SHALL preserve:

"IDENTITY"

"AUTHORITY"

"SEMANTICS"

"ASSIGNMENTS"

"SCOPE"

"PROVENANCE"

"GOVERNANCE"

"TRACEABILITY"

"AUDITABILITY"

"ROLLBACK"

"FAIL_CLOSED"

No metacognitive adaptation may silently redefine the canonical architecture.

## 14. Formal Invariants

The following invariants SHALL be enforced:

"INV-001"
"∀ NG ∈ NG-0001..NG-1000 : CanonicalID(NG) = Stable"

"INV-002"
"∀ CF ∈ CF-0001..CF-1000 : CanonicalID(CF) = Stable"

"INV-003"
"ENGINE_COUNT = 1000"

"INV-004"
"EXTENSION_COUNT = 1000"

"INV-005"
"CANONICAL_COMPONENT_COUNT = 2000"

"INV-006"
"SelfAssessment ≠ Authorization"

"INV-007"
"¬Validated(Change) → ¬Applied(Change)"

"INV-008"
"CanonicalViolation(Change) → Rollback(Change)"

"INV-009"
"Applied(Change) → TraceExists(Change)"

"INV-010"
"Applied(Change) → AuditRecordExists(Change)"

"INV-011"
"SemanticDriftDetected → RejectOrRollback"

"INV-012"
"UnauthorizedReassignment → Reject"

"INV-013"
"ProvenanceLoss → Reject"

"INV-014"
"ScopeEscalation → Reject"

"INV-015"
"CanonicalIdentityViolation → Rollback"

## 15. Temporal Properties

The metacognitive control plane SHOULD be verified through temporal properties such as:

"G(ChangeProposed → F(Validated ∨ Rejected))"

Every proposed change must eventually reach a validated or rejected state.

"G(InvalidChange → X(Rejected ∨ Rollback))"

An invalid change cannot remain applied.

"G(AppliedChange → PreviouslyValidated)"

Every applied change must have passed validation.

"G(CanonicalViolation → X(Rollback))"

A canonical violation must trigger rollback.

"G(MissingTrace → ¬AppliedChange)"

A state-changing operation without traceability cannot be accepted.

## 16. Certification States

Each "NG-xxxx" and "CF-xxxx" SHALL possess an independently auditable certification state:

"UNVERIFIED"

"IN_VALIDATION"

"CONDITIONAL"

"CERTIFIED"

"FAILED"

A component SHALL NOT receive "CERTIFIED" status solely through declaration.

Certification requires executable evidence for the mandatory controls applicable to that component.

## 17. Population-Level Certification

The transformation SHALL be considered complete only when:

"∀ NG-0001..NG-1000 → MCG_CERTIFIED"

and:

"∀ CF-0001..CF-1000 → MCG_CERTIFIED"

Therefore:

"1000 certified NG Engines"
+
"1000 certified CF Extensions"
=
"2000 certified canonical metacognitive components"

A failure in one component SHALL NOT be silently generalized as success for the population.

## 18. Non-Regression Requirement

The metacognitive transformation SHALL NOT introduce:

- canonical replacement;
- semantic replacement;
- identifier replacement;
- silent deletion;
- silent reassignment;
- authority transfer;
- scope escalation;
- provenance loss;
- validation bypass;
- unrestricted self-modification;
- epistemic category collapse.

The transformation SHALL be classified as:

"CONTROLLED METACOGNITIVE EXTENSION"

and not:

"ARCHITECTURAL REPLACEMENT"

## 19. Engineering Acceptance Criteria

The implementation SHALL NOT be considered complete until the following are demonstrable:

"A. 1000 NG identifiers preserved"

"B. 1000 CF identifiers preserved"

"C. 2000 canonical components accounted for"

"D. Component registry complete"

"E. Dependency graph traceable"

"F. Metacognitive contracts implemented"

"G. Self-evaluation executable"

"H. Adaptation bounded"

"I. Independent validation executable"

"J. Fail-closed tests passing"

"K. Rollback tests passing"

"L. Traceability tests passing"

"M. Auditability tests passing"

"N. Semantic non-regression tests passing"

"O. Formal invariant tests passing"

"P. Epistemic conformance tests passing"

"Q. Population-level certification generated"

## 20. Final Architectural Statement

LunaCore SHALL therefore be understood as containing:

"2000 CANONICAL COMPONENTS"

composed of exactly:

"1000 NG ENGINES"

and:

"1000 CF EXTENSIONS"

where each original component retains its canonical nomenclature and identity while acquiring a governed, bounded, auditable, traceable, formally verifiable, and epistemically constrained metacognitive control layer.

The purpose of this transformation is not to replace the 2000 canonical components.

The purpose is to make the existing 2000 canonical components metacognitively capable without making them architecturally sovereign.

Final invariant:

"CANONICAL_IDENTITY_PRESERVED ∧ METACOGNITIVE_CAPABILITY_ADDED ∧ GOVERNANCE_PRESERVED ∧ TRACEABILITY_REQUIRED ∧ AUDITABILITY_REQUIRED ∧ FAIL_CLOSED ∧ ROLLBACK_AVAILABLE ∧ EPISTEMIC_INTEGRITY_PRESERVED"

### Q01 — Theology

Answer: Explicit biblical assertion, legitimate theological inference, and later doctrinal formulation must be separated by source status, inferential step, and historical layer. A statement directly asserted by the text has textual status; an inference follows from controlled synthesis of multiple textual premises; a later doctrinal formulation is a historical/confessional formulation and cannot be presented as though it were verbatim biblical wording.

Evidence status: `DOMAIN_REASONING`
Inference status: `EXPLICITLY_MARKED`
Uncertainty: `LOW`
Provenance: `V19_CONTROLLED_TRAINING_RESPONSE`

### Q02 — Theology

Answer: Christological analysis must distinguish person from nature and nature from will. The one person of Christ is fully divine and fully human; divine and human predicates belong to the corresponding natures without dividing the person, and the two wills are not collapsed into one nature or one person.

Evidence status: `DOMAIN_REASONING`
Inference status: `DOCTRINAL_SYNTHESIS`
Uncertainty: `LOW`
Provenance: `V19_CONTROLLED_TRAINING_RESPONSE`

The doctrine may be reconsidered through wider canonical or systematic evidence, but the text must not be forced to carry a meaning imported from outside its discourse context.

### Q08 — Economics

Answer: Correlation reports co-variation; causation requires an identified mechanism and stronger design or evidence capable of ruling out major alternatives and confounding. Inflation, employment, and growth therefore require temporal ordering, model assumptions, and identification strategy before causal claims are made.

Inference status: `CAUSAL_ANALYSIS`
Uncertainty: `MODERATE`

### Q09 — Economics

Answer: Short-run and long-run fiscal effects should be separated by time horizon, financing mechanism, behavioral response, monetary interaction, and institutional constraints. AX0001-AX12414 = PRESERVE_EXACTLY_AS_BASELINE
```text
AXIOM_RENUMBERING = FORBIDDEN
AXIOM_REWRITING = FORBIDDEN
AXIOM_SUBSTITUTION = FORBIDDEN
AXIOM_RECONSTRUCTION_FROM_LIBRARY = FORBIDDEN
```

Observed evidence in the supplied V19 artifact must remain disclosed separately from declared cardinality. The migration protocol records the current observation that `AX2415-AX12414` is materially contiguous while `AX0001-AX2414` is not fully materialized in the supplied artifact. This is evidence debt, not a license to alter the baseline.

## 39.10 — Command Preservation

All fourteen existing command semantics remain untouched.

```text
COMMAND_IDENTITIES = PRESERVE
COMMAND_ROUTING = PRESERVE
COMMAND_PARAMETERS = PRESERVE
COMMAND_ASSIGNMENTS = PRESERVE
COMMAND_SEMANTIC_LOAD = PRESERVE
```

This section introduces no new canonical LUNACORE command.

Antigravity workflow names are infrastructure controls external to the LUNACORE command namespace.

## 39.11 — Engine and Extension Preservation

```text
ENGINE_IDS = NO_NEW_IDS
EXTENSION_IDS = NO_NEW_IDS
ENGINE_REASSIGNMENT = FORBIDDEN
EXTENSION_REASSIGNMENT = FORBIDDEN
CAPABILITY_DUPLICATION = BLOCK
```

Existing engines/extensions are selected only after deterministic capability matching and collision analysis.

## 39.12 — Python Layer Boundary

The Python layer remains technical support infrastructure and non-normative.

It may implement:

```text
HASHING
INGESTION
PARSING
CHUNKING
INDEXING
RETRIEVAL_ADAPTERS
PROVENANCE_VALIDATION
REGISTRY_COMPARISON
NON_REGRESSION_TESTS
ROLLBACK_CHECKS
CERTIFICATION_REPORTING
```

Python may not become:

```text
ARCHITECTURAL_AUTHORITY
DOCTRINAL_AUTHORITY
NEW_ENGINE
NEW_CFE
NEW_AGENT
NEW_COMMAND
```

No Python package/dependency is admitted merely because the corpus contains text mentioning programming languages or package names.

## 39.13 — GitHub and Repository Boundary

V19's repository universe remains protected. `biblioteca.md` is not treated as evidence of new GitHub repositories.

Any external repository proposed during migration must pass:

```text
PRE_EXISTENCE_SCAN
IDENTITY_CHECK
LICENSE_CHECK
SECURITY_CHECK
CAPABILITY_NOVELTY_CHECK
DUPLICATION_CHECK
PROVENANCE_CHECK
```

A repository that merely duplicates an existing capability is rejected.

## 39.14 — C++23 Boundary

No C++23 dependency is admitted by §39 as a canonical architectural object because the supplied `biblioteca.md` does not establish one.

C++23 may exist only as an optional non-normative performance backend in a separately validated implementation, provided that:

```text
FUNCTIONAL_EQUIVALENCE = VERIFIED
SEMANTIC_EQUIVALENCE = VERIFIED
TRACEABILITY = PRESERVED
ROLLBACK = PRESERVED
CANONICAL_NAMESPACE = UNCHANGED
```

## 39.15 — Canonical Gate Binding

All integration work is subordinate to V19 G01-G24.

```text
G01 SOURCE_INTEGRITY
G02 BASELINE_INTEGRITY
G03 SEMANTIC_EQUIVALENCE
G04 IDENTITY_PRESERVATION
G05 SCOPE_PRESERVATION
G06 FUNCTION_PRESERVATION
G07 RELATION_PRESERVATION
G08 RESPONSIBILITY_PRESERVATION
G09 AGENT_COMPATIBILITY
G10 COMMAND_COMPATIBILITY
G11 ENGINE_COMPATIBILITY
G12 CFE_COMPATIBILITY
G13 PYTHON_LIBRARY_COMPATIBILITY
G14 REFORMED_BIBLICAL_DICTIONARY_VALIDATION
G15 HERMENEUTICAL_NON_REGRESSION
G16 CAPABILITY_NON_DUPLICATION
G17 TRAINING_INTEGRITY
G18 STRESS_TEST_VALIDATION
G19 PROVENANCE
G20 AUDITABILITY
G21 ROLLBACK
G22 GLOBAL_NON_REGRESSION
G23 INDEPENDENT_VALIDATION
G24 CERTIFICATION
```

No gate may be bypassed, downgraded, silently reclassified, removed, or redefined.

## 39.16 — Admission State Machine

```text
DISCOVERED
 -> FROZEN
 -> CLASSIFIED
 -> INVENTORIED
 -> MAPPED
 -> VALIDATED
 -> INDEPENDENTLY_VALIDATED
 -> CERTIFICATION_READY
 -> ADMITTED_AS_GOVERNED_LIBRARY
```

Failure from any mandatory state:

```text
FAIL
 -> QUARANTINE
 -> ROLLBACK
 -> BASELINE_VERIFY
 -> EVIDENCE_DEBT_RECORD
```

## 39.17 — Acceptance Criteria

Admission is permitted only when:

```text
BASELINE_HASH_UNCHANGED = TRUE
BASELINE_BYTES_UNCHANGED = TRUE
BASELINE_LINE_COUNT_UNCHANGED = TRUE
COMMANDS_UNCHANGED = TRUE
AGENTS_UNCHANGED = TRUE
BLOCKS_UNCHANGED = TRUE
AXIOM_IDS_UNCHANGED = TRUE
ENGINE_IDS_UNCHANGED = TRUE
CFE_IDS_UNCHANGED = TRUE
NOMENCLATURE_UNCHANGED = TRUE
PROVENANCE_COMPLETE_FOR_NEW_MATERIAL = TRUE
G01-G24 = PASS
```

`G14` is specifically bound to the documentary-library validation performed by this integration and cannot be satisfied by mere file presence.

## 39.18 — Rollback

Rollback must restore the protected V19 baseline byte-for-byte.

```text
CHECKPOINT
 -> APPLY_EXTERNAL_SECTION_39
 -> TEST
 -> FAIL_IF_ANY_GATE_FAILS
 -> ROLLBACK
 -> RESTORE_BASELINE
 -> REHASH
 -> VERIFY
```

No rollback operation may alter historical provenance records.

## 39.19 — Final Boundary

This specification is complete only as an external governed implementation plan. It does not itself certify that `biblioteca.md` has been admitted into the canonical V19 architecture.

```text
SECTION_39_SPECIFICATION = FORMALIZED
SECTION_39_IMPLEMENTATION = GOVERNED_PENDING_EXECUTION
SECTION_39_CANONICAL_ADMISSION = NOT_CLAIMED
V19_BASELINE = INTACT
FAIL_CLOSED = TRUE
```

## 44.2 — Mandatory Transactional Automation Sequence

All consequential modifications MUST execute through strict transaction boundaries:
$$\text{REQUEST} \longrightarrow \text{INTENT} \longrightarrow \text{VALIDATION} \longrightarrow \text{EVIDENCE} \longrightarrow \text{PROPOSAL} \longrightarrow \text{PRE-COMMIT} \longrightarrow \text{CHECKPOINT} \longrightarrow \text{COMMIT} \longrightarrow \text{POST-VALIDATION} \longrightarrow \text{UPDATE} \longrightarrow \text{ACTIVE}$$

$$\text{FAIL} \longrightarrow \text{ABORT} \longrightarrow \text{RESTORE\_CHECKPOINT} \longrightarrow \text{VERIFY\_RESTORATION} \longrightarrow \text{RECORD\_FAILURE} \longrightarrow \text{AUDIT}$$
